Patients with stones in the common bile duct or acute chole- cystitis require prompt therapy because of the risk of serious complications; endoscopic sphincterotomy and physical retriev- al of the stones with a basket or balloon appears to be the pre- ferred treatment, with open surgery as an alternative. A biliary stent to allow bile flow around the stone has been used as a tem- porary measure in patients with stones too large to remove by endoscopic sphincterotomy. Lithotripsy or infusion of a solvent such as monoctanoin or methyl tert-butyl ether are possible alter- natives in patients unfit for surgery. In patients who develop cholecystitis or cholangitis antibacterial therapy may be required (see Biliary-tract Infections, p.164). References. 1. Johnston DE, Kaplan MM.
